question_record.context: A security incident involving unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth app was reported. The user Luciano Herrera (pwilson@niseko.alpineskihouse.co) performed the unusual addition of credentials to the application SimulandApp. This action may indicate a compromised app being used for malicious purposes such as spreading phishing, exfiltrating data, or gaining unauthorized access. Following this, there was a detection of a malicious PowerShell Cmdlet invoked on the machine. As part of these events, it was also detected that a user clicked on a potentially malicious URL.
question_record.question: Can you provide the mailbox primary address of the user who clicked on the detected malicious URL?
solution: The user with SID `S-1-5-21-551436448-9871687716-9837441745-1903` (Luciano Herrera) performed an unusual addition of credentials to the application SimulandApp. The credential type added was Password. This may indicate potential compromise of the app or Luciano Herrera's account.

A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked by the user with AadUserId `a2d0f7c2-b0a0-43bd-bce0-27d8ae3be4d0` on a machine. This could be associated with various malicious activities such as credential theft or exploitation.
A potentially malicious URL was clicked by the user with mailbox address `bjenkins@niseko.alpineskihouse.co`. This indicates that the user might have been targeted by a phishing attack.

80.name: Unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth app
80.description: The user Luciano Herrera (pwilson@niseko.alpineskihouse.co) performed an unusual addition of credentials to the application SimulandApp. This usage pattern may indicate that an attacker has compromised the app, and is using it to spread phishing, exfiltrate data, or to gain access to other accounts and devices. The user added a credential of type Password. A credential of type Password is added when an application is using a password to authenticate.

51.name: A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked on the machine
51.description: A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked on the machine. The Cmdlet may be associated with credential theft, exploitation, network reconnaissance or code injection.

104.name: A potentially malicious URL click was detected
104.description: We have detected that one of your users has recently clicked on a link that was found to be malicious. -V1.0.0.5

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Account_Derived_Email' AND o.Concept = 'Account_SID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
